title: Ben Johnson on Bears' victory over Eagles | Press Conference
headline: Case Keenum earned the start in the 27-7 win over the Eagles and played well; Caleb Williams' status for next week is an open question.
summary: Johnson praised the team for bouncing back after its first loss, crediting preparation and a clean game with only five penalties. He said the defense was outstanding in the second half, with three takeaways and a plan that the coaches taught well, though he declined to single out one player. Offensively, the running game was slow early, so the team leaned on the passing game, which Johnson credited to Keenum's quick decisions, efficiency and ball security. He said Keenum ran the pregame quarterback meeting himself and called the week's choice an accumulation of practice reps, not a single moment. Johnson called the two-point sneak a Mike Martz-style play that worked after the defense stemmed late. Asked about next week, he said the staff would discuss it if Caleb Williams can't play, and he reaffirmed that Tyson Bagent is the number two quarterback. He also said Cam Lewis has a hip issue and the team will see how he progresses on a short week.

injuries.detail: Johnson said Lewis has a hip problem and the staff will monitor his progress ahead of a short week; no designation was given.

signals.note: Keenum's strong efficient performance makes him the clear alternative starter if Williams is out.
signals.quote: He played lights out.

signals.claim: Bagent is the team's number two quarterback behind Williams and Keenum
signals.note: Bagent is the backup option if Williams is out and Keenum is not starting, though Johnson did not name him directly as next week's starter.
signals.quote: is our number two quarterback.

signals.claim: Williams' availability for next week is uncertain and the staff will decide the starter after discussion
signals.note: Johnson did not confirm an injury but did not rule out Williams missing time, which matters for Williams and Keenum managers.
signals.quote: we'll have a discussion as a coaching staff

topics.detail: Johnson said the running game struggled early and the team stuck with it, eventually getting some production late in the game.
The defense played strongly in the second half and created takeaways, with Johnson saying the unit played together as one and focused on continuing that trend.
Johnson called the game the team's cleanest of the season with only five penalties, which he said was a big deal.
Johnson said the final play of the first half was close and he would need to see it again before judging whether the clock hit zero.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference : September 29th, 2026
headline: Elgton Jenkins is in concussion protocol with a short week ahead; if he can't play, Luke Wypler is the likely replacement, with a backup behind him.
summary: Monken said the team is preparing for a Thursday game against Pittsburgh on a short week, and he framed the prime-time schedule as a positive for the players. Elgton Jenkins is in the concussion protocol, and if he can't clear it, Monken expects Luke Wypler to start in his place. He named a backup but the name was garbled in the captions, so it is not listed. Monken said the team walked through its practices Wednesday and will jog Thursday, with only some full-speed work, to keep players fresh. He praised Jared Verse's pass rush and said the defense's pocket pressure disrupted the opposing quarterback even without sacks. On Deshaun Watson's mobility, Monken said the team is fine with the current approach, since much of his scrambling happened organically, and he expects improvement as the offense plays around him more. Monken also said the team's young receivers and offensive linemen are still learning complex systems and that penalties and operational mistakes are being worked on. Tylan Wallace's status is unknown, with no update yet.

Monken had no update and said the timeline for news is still uncertain.

topics.detail: The team walked through practice on Wednesday and will jog Thursday with limited full-speed work, with a focus on getting bodies right for a Thursday night game.

Monken described Pittsburgh's new defensive staff as strong and noted the teams have had frequent matchups in recent years. He also praised Jaylen Warren as a hard-to-tackle back who catches well out of the backfield, and he praised T.J. Watt's ongoing production.

Monken said the team's penalties and operational mistakes stemmed from a new system and young players still learning nuances, and that the staff is working to fix communication and substitution issues.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “I’m Better Than That” | Press Conference
headline: Schottenheimer owns the late-game collapse; Jaishawn Barham keeps gaining ground, Jalen Thompson is out at least four weeks, and Jonathan Bullard is likely out a couple of weeks.
summary: Schottenheimer took full responsibility for the final 28 seconds against Baltimore, saying he overcoached Dak Prescott on third down by using a word that pushed him into a more conservative mindset. He said the breakdown carried into the kicking decision and that communication with the coordinators in that sequence was not good enough, which he called his fault. He described the Cowboys' two losses as failures to finish games and said the defense is giving up too many points, with weak edge containment, sloppy tackling and a lack of pass rush as the main issues. He praised Jaishawn Barham's growth at linebacker, saying he has made fewer mistakes than in the Giants game and is making a strong case to stay on the field. On injuries, Jonathan Bullard has a calf strain, Jalen Thompson is expected to miss at least four weeks, Von Miller and DeMarvion Overshown could return to practice this week, Malik Hooker is progressing well, and Cobie Durant will likely miss this week. Tyler Smith is progressing in rehab and could be a candidate for the Thursday game. The team held personnel discussions and a workout for potential defensive signings, and he said Goodson and Demercado both have value at running back and special teams.

topics.detail: Schottenheimer took responsibility for the final 28 seconds and the third-down overcoaching of Dak Prescott, saying he will not repeat the mistake. He said the coordinator communication failed and that the game management process will not change.
He said the run defense and third-down play improved, but perimeter containment, tackling and pass rush must get better. He said the team is giving up too many points.
The team held a workout with potential signings to add bodies because of injuries, especially on defense. Personnel talks are a regular Monday or Tuesday part of the week.

Schottenheimer said his conversation with Jerry Jones was productive and that Jones understood the mistake.

title: HC Jeff Hafley - Sept 28 | Press Conference
headline: De'Von Achane faces surgery with no date set, so expect a committee backfield of Ollie Gordon, Malik Washington, and DJ Herman; Jaylen Wright and Caleb Douglas are day-to-day.
summary: Hafley said he was heartbroken for De'Von Achane, praising his growth, leadership, and energy, and said he expects him to return strong. Achane's surgery is already scheduled, but the date isn't set and more details are expected Tuesday. Hafley said the backfield will be shared by committee, with Ollie Gordon, Malik Washington, and DJ Herman all earning roles, and that the run game remains the identity. He credited the offensive line and said the run game worked well against a strong defense. Jaylen Wright is day-to-day after being held out, and Caleb Douglas is also day-to-day, with updates expected Wednesday. On defense, Hafley said the safety pairing of Dante Trader and Michael Taaffe will stay, and Jackson Woodard has been used in nickel for his physicality. He also discussed penalties that negated scoring plays, a slow start that allowed opening-drive scores, and Malik Willis' improving decision-making alongside a ball-security issue.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: September 28, 2026
headline: Jalen Hurts briefly left after a sideline hit and returned; Sirianni says the offense's negative plays and minus-seven turnover margin must be fixed.
summary: Sirianni took ownership of the loss, saying the Eagles were not ready to coach or play and that the defeat falls on him. He admitted he should have gone for it on fourth-and-one earlier and called his decision there one he wants back. He said he had no information on Jalen Hurts when Hurts went to the sideline after a hit, and he chose not to call a timeout so the medical process could run its course. He defended Hurts's late-half decision-making, saying he trusted him to make the right call, which led to a touchdown. Sirianni said the offense stalled in the second half because of negative plays, including backward runs and off-schedule downs, and that short passes have struggled because of number-count issues, missed blocks, and execution. He cited a minus-seven turnover margin as a key reason the team cannot sustain wins, and said the defense also needs review on tape. He also said he regretted his emotional reaction to the sideline hit on Hurts and believes he must stay more composed.

injuries.detail: Left briefly after a hit on the sideline and was evaluated; he returned to the game and led a late touchdown drive. Sirianni said he had no medical information during the stoppage.

signals.claim: Hurts was hit on the sideline and went through evaluation before returning to the game.
signals.note: Hurts returned, but the sideline hit is worth monitoring for any lingering effects in practice this week.
signals.quote: Obviously you never want to see your quarterback get hit like that

signals.claim: Sirianni trusts Hurts to make late-game decisions, including the clock-management choices that set up the touchdown.
signals.note: Sirianni's trust in Hurts' end-of-half decision-making supports his continued control of two-minute situations.
signals.quote: I trust him in those situations to make the right decision.

topics.detail: Sirianni said he should have gone for it on fourth-and-one and called his fourth-and-five decision a fourth-and-one-and-a-half situation in hindsight. He called the fourth-and-one jump-offside attempt a decision he wants back.

Sirianni said the run game had success in the first half but the offense went backward with holds and negative plays, and short passes have not worked this year due to number counts, missed blocks, and execution. He said the offense needs to fix these fundamentals.
Sirianni said the team is minus seven in turnover margin, which he says makes sustaining wins very difficult. He also pointed to pre-snap penalties and secondary penalties as problems to fix.
Sirianni said the defense will be reviewed on tape, with a focus on missed opportunities, but said the loss was not just the offense or defense.
Sirianni credited the Bears' quarterback, offensive line, and coaching staff, saying the Eagles were outcoached and outplayed.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Sept. 29)
headline: Coach McCarthy gave no named injury update on the short-week Thursday trip to Cleveland. He called Aaron Rodgers a key asset for the noisy road environment and said the offense is still growing into its concepts.
summary: McCarthy spoke before a Thursday-schedule practice ahead of a short-week game in Cleveland. He was asked about a player's first full practice participation and said they hope he plays, but would not commit to a full workload until Friday's full-speed session. On the injury report, he said several players are working through things, but that the morning update was that everyone was making progress and he hopes to have everybody Thursday. He said the later practice start lets players sleep and coaches finish game planning. He praised first-year lineman Max Iheanachor's composure in his first career start and said pre-snap operation is a focus for the Cleveland crowd. He said Aaron Rodgers's experience in loud road games makes him a key asset for operating in the noise. McCarthy said the offense has not yet been over 70 plays in a game and is working through concepts, and he is trying to balance creativity with less volume.

signals.claim: Will be a key asset in operating the offense in the loud Cleveland environment
signals.note: McCarthy frames Rodgers's road and prime-time experience as central to the Thursday game plan, which supports his usual passing-game role.

signals.claim: Looked composed in his first career start; pre-snap operation is a focus for the Cleveland game
signals.note: Offensive line depth-chart context only, with little direct fantasy value.
signals.quote: I think things come very natural to Max

topics.detail: McCarthy said several players are working through things, and the injury report will come out after practice. A player described as a full participant for the first time is not named by the coach, so his status for the week is unclear.
Thursday-schedule practice runs as a jog-through with a faster pace and similar reps. Full-speed work is planned for Friday, which will guide decisions on the player's workload.
McCarthy declined to say how a possible return would change the defensive plan. He said matchups and personnel groupings will decide slot versus outside alignments on the short week.

McCarthy said the offense is still learning concepts, that third-down issues were the main problem early, and that first-down production improved last week. He wants to balance fewer, more creative plays with productivity.
